current.text: Brooklyn recently signed him to a contract extension.
He is left out of the projected 10-man rotation. A crowded Nets frontcourt hurts his chance at a real role.
Brooklyn's projected bench rotation is Keon Ellis, Noah Clowney, Mo Wagner, Danny Wolf and Nolan Traore. Three of them are big men.
He is one of Brooklyn's best upside prospects and is a stash option in case the Nets give young players minutes late in the season.
Houston controls Brooklyn's draft pick, so the Nets have no reason to tank.
The Nets' second half is uncertain. They could hand more minutes to young players like Minott, and Michael Porter Jr. could be traded.
Brooklyn is projected to be one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins.
Brooklyn plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21, with one back-to-back in that span. It has 16 back-to-backs this season, tied with Boston for the most in the league.

durable.text: He rates in the 91st percentile in DARKO.
He has always made an impact on the court, but he needs minutes to matter in fantasy.

note: He is not a draft target: Yahoo values him at 0 USD and ranks him 318th, well outside the 144 players our league drafts, and he went undrafted in our league last season. The upside case is minutes. In his last nine games last season he played 23 minutes and averaged 14 points, 1.4 steals and a block. Yahoo projects only 0.2 steals, which does not match that stretch. Leave him on waivers and watch for a Porter trade or more young-player minutes after the deadline.
